- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) but sentiment is weak, reduce slope by 20–40% to avoid overconfidence.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7); model should average 1–2 days of prior price + sentiment-weighted drift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often fails to capture bottoming; add 1–2% buffer below recent low.  
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
